parts.title: Who God is

runs: The Bible does not open with a proof that God exists. It opens with God already at work, making the world (
). Paul says the world itself points to its Maker:
Creation shows that God is powerful. It does not show what He is like toward us. For that the Bible gives His words and actions, and two things stand out.
God is
. Abraham, pleading for a city, asks: “Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?” (
). God does not shrug at wrong. A judge who ignored cruelty would not be good.
God is also
, and His love is not a feeling held at a distance. It acts: “God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son” (
). The Son is Jesus. Christians believe in one God, who is eternally Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Read more in the site’s article

parts.title: What went wrong

runs: The Bible’s word for what went wrong is
. Sin is not only breaking rules. It is turning away from God to run our lives our own way. The breaking of rules follows from that.
“All” includes the religious and the irreligious, the decent and the notorious. Nobody is ranked here. The verse puts every reader in the same place.

Isaiah describes the same thing with a picture from farm life. Jewish readers, from the medieval commentator Rashi onward, usually take the suffering “servant” of these chapters to be the people of Israel. Isaiah himself calls Israel God’s servant (
). Christians, following the New Testament (
), read the servant as Jesus. Either way, the verse’s description of us is plain:
means wrongdoing.) Read more in
The cost is serious: “For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord” (
). Look at the two halves. Death is earned, like a wage. Life is a gift.
in the Bible means more than living forever. It is life with God, beginning now and never ending.
this part names the problem. It does not ask you to feel a certain amount of guilt before you may go on reading. Read more in

consider: , which half is earned, and which is given?
reflect: Where in your own life have you “turned to your own way”? Name it honestly, to yourself.

parts.title: Three lost things

runs: Jesus told these stories because people were complaining about the company He kept.
were Jews who collected taxes for the Roman occupiers, and many people saw them as traitors and cheats. The
were a movement of devout Jews who took God’s law seriously in daily life, and the
were teachers of that law. Their complaint was a reasonable-sounding one: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them” (
). Jesus answers it with three
, short stories that make one picture carry a truth.
A shepherd loses one sheep out of a hundred and goes after it “until he finds it” (
). A woman loses one coin out of ten, lights a lamp and sweeps “until she finds it” (
). In both stories the one who owns the lost thing goes looking for it. The sheep does not find its own way home. And both stories end in a party: “Rejoice with me” (

The third story is longer. A younger son asks for his inheritance early, leaves, and spends it all. In a famine he ends up feeding pigs, which was a bitter disgrace for a Jewish listener. Then “he came to his senses” (
). He plans a speech: he has sinned, he is not worthy, he will ask to be a hired servant (
). This is what the Bible means by
. It means to turn: to change your mind about yourself and about God, and then to head back home.
Look closely at what the son says when he arrives. He begins his speech, but the request to be made a hired servant never comes out (compare
with
). The father interrupts with a robe, a ring, sandals and a feast. “For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!” (
Then the story turns to the older brother, who “became angry and refused to go in” (
). He had stayed and worked, and he resents the welcome. His father “came out and pleaded with him” (
). The story ends with the father’s plea, and we never learn whether the older son went in. Jesus told it to the grumblers of verse 2. It leaves them, and us, at the door.

a parable is a picture, not a complete account. This one shows God’s welcome. It does not explain how God can welcome sinners and still be just; Acts 2 and Romans 3 take that up below. Read the parables more widely in

consider: In each of the three stories, who does the searching or the running? How does the father answer each son?
reflect: Are you more like the son far away, or the son who stayed and is angry outside? Both are invited in.

parts.title: Who Jesus is, and what He did

runs: About seven weeks after Jesus was put to death, Jerusalem was full of pilgrims for
, the Feast of Weeks. This Jewish festival falls fifty days after Passover, and Greek-speaking Jews called it Pentecost. On that day Jesus’ followers were filled with the Holy Spirit (
; read more in
). Peter, a Jew speaking to his fellow Jews, explained what had happened.
Peter says three things about Jesus in a few lines. God showed who Jesus was through His works. Jesus’ death was not an accident: “He was delivered up by God’s set plan and foreknowledge” (
). And death could not hold Him: “God raised Him from the dead … because it was impossible for Him to be held in its clutches” (
). The
means that Jesus came back to bodily life, and did not merely survive as a memory.
Peter then reads Israel’s own Scriptures, the Psalms of David, as pointing to this:
is the place of the dead.) Read more in
. Peter’s sermon reaches its point:
is the Greek form of the Hebrew
, “anointed one”: the King God had promised.
is the title of the one who has the right to rule.
Peter said “you crucified” as a Jew to a Jerusalem crowd, and he named the Romans as “the hands of the lawless” (

). Weeks later the first believers prayed that “Herod and Pontius Pilate conspired with the Gentiles and the people of Israel against Your holy servant Jesus” and that “they carried out what Your hand and will had decided beforehand would happen” (
). Isaiah says the LORD laid on Him “the iniquity of us all” (
). Scripture places the guilt for Christ’s death on all of us. It never places it on the Jewish people as a people, and this site never does.

parts.title: Turn and trust

runs: The crowd did not hear Peter’s sermon as interesting information. “They were cut to the heart and asked Peter and the other apostles, ’Brothers, what shall we do?’” (
). The
were the people Jesus personally sent out with His message.
The promise is wide: “to you and your children and to all who are far off” (
). That includes people far from Jerusalem and far from God. “Those who embraced his message were baptized” (
): they embraced the message first, and the water came after. The question about baptism is answered below.
Paul puts the same response in other words:
To
, or have
, here means to trust, the way you trust a bridge by putting your weight on it. To be
) means to be declared right by God, as a judge declares someone in the right. That is how a person is made right with God. It is not earned. It is
, God’s kindness given to people who do not deserve it. “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved” (
). In the prophet Joel, “the Lord” in those words is the LORD, Israel’s God (
). Paul applies them to Jesus.

No form of words saves anyone. A prayer can express faith. You may tell God, in your own words, that you have sinned, that you believe Jesus died and rose, and that you are trusting Him as Lord. But it is God who saves, through faith in Christ, and not the words. If you have trusted Him, you do not need to wonder whether you said it correctly.

parts.title: What happens next

runs: The new believers in Acts 2 did not stay alone. They were baptized and “added to the believers” (
). Three things follow for anyone who trusts Christ.

blocks.label: Baptism
runs: is going under water, in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, as a public sign that you belong to Christ. Baptists call it an

, a practice Jesus ordered His followers to keep. With the Baptist Faith and Message, this site holds that baptism is “the immersion of a believer in water”, and “an act of obedience symbolizing the believer’s faith” (article VII, baptism and the Lord’s Supper).
reads each baptism in Acts.

blocks.label: The Bible
runs: Begin with one of the Gospels, the four accounts of Jesus’ life. Mark is short, and John was written so that readers would believe (
). This suggestion is the site’s, not a rule.
And you can know where you stand:
John writes “so that you may
”. This kind of confidence, called
, rests on God’s word about His Son, not on how strong your feelings are today. Read more in

questions.title: Is it too late for me?

runs: If you are asking this because you feel you have gone too far, or you are thinking of ending your life, please speak to someone today. In the United States, call or text 988. In Spain, call 024. In Mexico, the Línea de la Vida is 800 911 2000. In Brazil, CVV answers on 188. For other countries, see
. Anywhere, you can call your local emergency number. Feelings this heavy do pass, and people do recover. Telling someone is the right thing to do.

As long as you are alive to ask, it is not too late. The son in Luke 15 had wasted everything, and his father ran to him. One of the men crucified beside Jesus had nothing left to offer, and Jesus promised him Paradise that day (
). “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved” (
). The word
has no exceptions.
Turning to Christ does not mean despising the people who raised you. God’s own commandments tell us to honour father and mother (
). If your family is Jewish, remember that Peter was a Jew speaking to Jews, and that Jesus is presented to them as Israel’s own promised Messiah (
). Paul writes, “there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him” (

Faith cannot be inherited or forced. The Baptist Faith and Message holds that God alone is Lord of the conscience (article XVII, religious liberty). Take your time, ask your questions, and speak to your family with respect. The site’s
treat other religions in their own words.

questions.title: Must I be baptized to be saved?

runs: Baptists answer no. People are saved by grace through faith in Christ (
). The man on the cross was promised Paradise, and Luke records no baptism (
). In
, the Spirit came on believers before any water. Baptists read “for the forgiveness of your sins” in

as joining faith and its first public act, because in Acts baptism followed belief closely. Baptism does not save. It is obedience, and it shows in public what has already happened. That does not make it optional for a believer, because Jesus commanded it.
Other Christians read it differently. Luther’s Small Catechism, a Lutheran teaching, says of baptism that “It worketh forgiveness of sins”. It is shown here as theirs.

questions.title: Why would a loving God judge anyone?

runs: A God who never judged would be a God who did not care about the abused, the cheated and the murdered. His justice is part of His love. The question is how a just God can forgive at all, and the cross is where both are kept:
God “presented Him as the atoning sacrifice” (
). An
is one that takes away guilt and makes peace with God. God does not ignore sin. In Christ He bears it Himself. Read more in
This is not a claim Christians invented to feel superior. Jesus made it about Himself:
Peter, on trial, said the same: “Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved” (

). With the Baptist Faith and Message, this site holds that “There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ as Lord” (article IV, salvation). That is said humbly. No Christian found the way by their own goodness. Like the sheep in Luke 15, they were found.

questions.title: What about those who never heard?

runs: Scripture gives us solid ground here, not every detail. The Judge of all the earth will do what is right (
). Everyone has some light. Creation shows God’s “eternal power and divine nature” (
), and conscience bears witness, “their thoughts either accusing or defending them on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus” (
). Paul does not say that this light saves. He says it leaves no one without witness.
This site will not promise more than Scripture says. What it does say is why Christians go: Paul goes on to ask how people can call on someone they have never heard of (

). The Baptist Faith and Message calls every believer to “endeavor to make disciples of all nations” (article XI, evangelism and missions). If you have now heard, the question is not only about them. Read more in

study.title: The good news
study.subtitle: how a person is made right with God
lead: This study is for you if you are not a Christian, or are not sure what Christians actually believe. It reads a few passages to answer one question: how can a person be put right with God? It teaches one habit for reading them: before you ask what you must do, ask what God has done.
frame: , which Christians use often, means “good news”. News is a report of something that has already happened. Advice tells you what to do. The Bible does give commands, but the message at its centre is news: God has acted, in history, through Jesus. So as you read, look first for what God has done. Ask what you should do only after that. The passages below are written in this order, and so is this study.
selection: This is a selection, not a census. The Bible says far more about God, sin and salvation than one page can hold. This study walks two passages fully. The first is three stories Jesus told in Luke 15. The second is the first public sermon about Jesus after His death, in Acts 2. It quotes a few other verses along the way and links to the studies that read them fully. Six questions readers often ask are answered at the end.

close.title: Ask what God has done
way: Here is the habit to carry to the next passage. Read the gospel as news before you read it as advice. Ask first what God has done: in the shepherd who searches, the father who runs, the Jesus God raised. Then ask what it calls for. Turn, trust, and come in.
invite: If you have not yet trusted Christ, none of this begins with you getting yourself in order. It begins with Him. The father in Luke 15 ran before his son finished speaking. Turn from your sin and trust Jesus as Lord, because “There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ as Lord”. Tell Him so, in your own words. Then find a church, tell someone there, and ask to be baptized.
question: Which son are you, the one far away or the one standing outside, and what would it take for you to go in?
again: Read the passage again before you answer.

news.news: God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son
news.note: The giving comes before the believing, in the same sentence.

news.news: his father came out and pleaded with him
news.note: The father goes out to the son who will not come in. Jesus does not say what the son did.

news.news: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ
news.note: The crowd asks what to do only after Peter has told them what God has done.

news.news: God raised Him from the dead
news.note: What you believe is something God has already done.

news.news: it is the gift of God
news.note: Faith receives a gift. It does not earn one.

news.news: God presented Him as the atoning sacrifice
news.response: the one who has faith in Jesus
news.note: God keeps His justice and still justifies.

news.news: God has given us eternal life
news.response: so that you may know that you have eternal life
news.note: Assurance rests on what God has given, not on a feeling.
